first.rationale: The situation shows concurrent declines in both activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory 31 and 86 both demonstrate that reducing friction in onboarding has produced durable, measurable lifts in activation and completion metrics. Verifying these two memories is prudent because they directly address the observed degradation and represent the most lower-risk lever available. While promotional pricing could compete for the SMB segment, it risks margin erosion and doesn't address the activation decline. Enterprise sales assist targets a different segment entirely. Referral incentives work on established customers, not new acquisition. Activation messaging is worthwhile but onboarding simplification addresses a demonstrable upstream bottleneck. A standard experiment with simplified onboarding can be run, measured, and iterated within the week, targeting both observed metrics with a well-established lever. The referral incentive memory (57) is strong but less relevant to the immediate problem statement. Preserving uncertainty: we are treating the durable memory as reliable but acknowledging that week-level competitive pressure and seasonal factors may interact differently than in the archived test conditions.
